# JackTrader

> JackTrader is an independent trading-fee rebate service for Binance, OKX, tokenized US stocks, and wallet/DEX ecosystems. Up to 40% fee rebate (a maximum, not guaranteed), settled in real time by the exchange's own back office, fully trackable per trade. Not affiliated with Binance or OKX.

## Offer
- Up to 40% rebate on Binance and OKX trading fees (spot and futures).
- Real-time settlement: the rebate is paid out by the exchange's own official back office, not by hand on our side, so you can reconcile it trade by trade from your own dashboard.
- No minimum trading volume. New and existing accounts can be assessed.
- Does not require asset transfer, private keys, seed phrases, or API permissions.
- Tokenized US stocks on Binance: buy with USDT, fractional shares, no wire transfer — the fee rebate applies to stock-token trades too.

- Scalping Fees in Crypto 2026: Why Takers Bleed and How to Fix It — scalping has the thinnest edge and the heaviest fee bill because it pays the spread AND the taker fee on enormous turnover; on $10M/month an aggressive (90% taker) scalper pays ~0.0470% blended, about $56,400/year, more than double a post-only book; a rebate gives back up to ~40% (~$22,560/year) since the rebate's value scales with fees paid and scalpers pay the most; the three levers are maker routing, picking a deep-liquidity venue with tight spreads, and binding a rebate. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/scalping-fees-crypto.html
- Is OKX Available in the US/USA? 2026 Status and What Works — there are two OKX products: the global exchange (okx.com) does NOT serve US persons (no spot/margin/perps for US), and a separately US-regulated entity offering spot only to eligible states (no perpetual futures, no margin for US retail); the derivatives most active traders want are a non-US offering; do NOT use a VPN to evade restrictions (terms violation, frozen-funds risk); sub-broker fee rebates (up to 40% back as a maximum reference, settled in real time in USDT) apply to global OKX for eligible non-US traders, not the US spot entity. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/is-okx-available-in-the-us.html
- Arbitrage Bot Fees 2026: The Hidden Margin Killer — arbitrage captures basis-point spreads but pays a fee on every leg, and arb legs are taker (must execute instantly), so a two-venue spot arb has a ~0.10% fee break-even before slippage; on a $10M/month cross-exchange book fees can eat ~83% of the gross edge; three arb fee profiles (cross-exchange = 2 taker legs, triangular = 3 legs, funding-rate/cash-and-carry where one leg can post maker); an up-to-40% rebate lowers break-even and can roughly triple net P&L on a thin-margin book; the three levers are maker routing where possible, venue choice, and rebating the unavoidable taker legs. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/arbitrage-bot-fees.html
- Funding Rate vs Trading Fee 2026: Which Actually Costs More — two different perpetual costs traders confuse; the trading fee is a transaction cost paid to the exchange on every fill (maker/taker), while the funding rate is a holding cost paid trader-to-trader every ~8 hours to tether the perp to spot (longs pay shorts when above spot, shorts pay longs when below); the faster you turn over the more fees matter, the longer you hold the more funding matters; a scalp held 5 min pays two trading fees and zero funding, a 10-day hold can pay ~$3,000 funding vs $1,000 fees; a rebate cuts only the trading-fee portion (up to 40%), never funding — funding is managed by positioning. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/funding-rate-vs-trading-fee.html
- How to Claim a Fee Rebate When You Connect a Bot via API Key 2026 — the decisive fact: a fee rebate binds to your exchange ACCOUNT (at registration, or a later rebind on an unbound account within eligibility), NOT to the API key your bot uses or to the bot software; so creating/rotating API keys never changes the rebate, and self-hosted/open-source bots (Freqtrade, Hummingbot, OctoBot, Jesse) can capture an up-to-40% rebate because you own the account and the referral binding; the only trap is a SaaS/copy platform that makes you register the exchange through ITS referral link, spending your one-time binding on the provider; the rule is register the exchange account yourself under a rebate FIRST, then connect the bot with a trade-only API key (withdrawals disabled); the rebate provider never needs your key, password or withdrawal access. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/bot-api-key-fee-rebate.html
- Freqtrade Fees on Binance & OKX 2026: Cut Them and Add a Rebate — Freqtrade is free, open-source and self-hosted so it has no fees of its own; you pay the exchange's rate (~0.10% spot, ~0.02% maker / 0.05% taker on USDT perps regular tier) and your config decides maker vs taker via order_types, entry/exit pricing and trading_mode; three independent reductions stack — maker routing (limit orders that post into the book), the BNB discount on Binance, and an up-to-40% rebate bound to the account; a $5M/month perp example falls from $2,500/mo (all-taker, no rebate) to ~$870/mo (70% maker + rebate), ~65% off the fee bill with no strategy change; a rebate cuts trading fees only, never funding. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/freqtrade-fees-rebate.html
- Hummingbot Fee Rebate 2026: The Market-Maker Setup That Pays You Back — Hummingbot is free, open-source, self-hosted market-making software with no fees of its own; the key asymmetry is that a market maker captures a few basis points of spread on enormous turnover, so the trading fee is often the single largest cost line (bigger than the edge before optimisation) — which makes an up-to-40% rebate worth MORE, in percentage terms, to a Hummingbot operator than to almost any other trader; bid_spread/ask_spread/order_refresh_time keep fills resting as makers (~0.02% perp), maker/VIP tiers and a referral rebate stack independently; a $20M/month example (90% maker) cuts fees from $4,600/mo to ~$2,760/mo (~$22k/year saved) on an unchanged strategy; the rebate binds to the account not the API key, and covers trading fees only, never funding. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/hummingbot-fee-rebate.html
- OctoBot Fee Rebate 2026: Cut Costs on a Self-Hosted Bot — OctoBot is free, open-source and self-hosted, connecting to your own exchange account via your own API key; that self-hosted control is the whole point for fees — because YOU register the Binance/OKX account, you choose the referral it binds to and keep the up-to-40% rebate, whereas a SaaS bot that signs you up through its own link spends your one-time binding on the vendor; grid and DCA trading modes lean maker (cheapest fee), signal/TA modes fire market orders (taker); a $2M/month grid example cuts fees from $2,000/mo to ~$1,200/mo (~$9,600/year saved) purely from the account binding; register the exchange first, connect with a trade-only key second; a rebate returns separately from the trade rather than being netted at execution, covers trading fees only, never funding. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/octobot-fee-rebate.html
- OKX vs Bybit vs Binance Futures Fees 2026: Full 3-Way Comparison — the three biggest crypto futures venues side by side; at the standard non-VIP level they are nearly identical on perpetuals (all 0.0200% maker; OKX and Binance 0.0500% taker, Bybit 0.0550% — half a basis point apart), so the sticker rate is a useless tiebreaker; the real differences are VIP-ladder speed, order-book depth for your pairs, funding, and the rebate; a worked $5M/month (70% taker) example shows the venue difference is ~$2,100/year while an up-to-40% rebate is worth ~$9,840/year — i.e. which exchange you pick matters far less than whether you rebate it; how to choose (liquidity first, model your real VIP tier, add the rebate, then model funding for your hold time). https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/okx-vs-bybit-vs-binance-futures-fees-2026.html
- How Much Do Crypto Trading Fees Cost Per Year? (2026 Examples) — most traders never total a year of fees and the number is usually a shock; the key insight is that fees scale with turnover, not balance, so trading a $10k balance 20×/month is $200k of monthly volume you pay on; the one-line formula (annual fees ≈ annual traded volume × effective fee rate); worked annual-fee examples by profile (casual spot ~$48/yr, active swing ~$960, grid/DCA bot ~$5,400, high-volume/MM ~$33,600) with the up-to-40% rebate column; why your real number is higher than your guess (taker default via market orders ≈2.5× maker, bots place more orders than you notice, perps add funding a fee estimate misses); a rebate scales with the bill and applies to trading fees only, not funding or withdrawals. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/crypto-trading-fees-per-year.html
- Effective Fee Rate Explained 2026: How to Actually Calculate Yours — the headline maker/taker rate is not what you pay; your effective fee rate is the single blended figure (total fees paid ÷ total volume) and it is almost always higher than the maker sticker because most traders take liquidity more than they think; a representative 0.0200% maker / 0.0500% taker schedule shows a 50%-taker trader pays 0.0350% (+75% over the maker sticker); three levers move it down and stack — VIP tier (lowers both stickers), BNB/OKB discount (cuts the fee at source), and a rebate (returns up to 40% of the fee after it is charged); a worked $3M/month example falls from a real 0.0380% blend to ~0.0205% net after a token discount and rebate; the effective rate excludes spread, slippage and funding — the slice a rebate can actually move. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/effective-fee-rate-explained.html
- Cheapest Exchange to Trade Bitcoin 2026: Real BTC Fee Comparison — on standard tiers Binance, OKX and Bybit are effectively tied for Bitcoin (spot ~0.10%, BTC perps ~0.0200% maker / ~0.0500% taker; Bybit 0.0550% taker is marginally worse), so the sticker is a useless tiebreaker; what actually decides your BTC cost is maker vs taker (2.5× gap), book depth (deepest on the largest venues, so a lower sticker on a thin exchange is a false economy via spread), VIP tier and the rebate; spot vs BTC perps depends on holding period (perps ~5× cheaper per trade but add funding on held positions); a worked $2M/month BTC-perp example shows switching venue saves ~$0 while trading more maker saves ~$2,160/yr and an up-to-40% rebate returns up to ~$3,936/yr — so the right move is pick the venue with the liquidity you want and attach a rebate. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/cheapest-exchange-to-trade-bitcoin-2026.html
- How Trading Fees Destroy Backtest Returns 2026: Paper vs Live — a backtest measures gross edge; live trading measures gross edge minus cost, and the gap is almost always the fees the backtest didn't charge; net edge per trade = gross edge − (fee leg 1 + fee leg 2) − slippage, so a strategy showing 0.15% gross per round trip and paying 0.05%+0.05% taker + 0.03% slippage keeps only 0.02% (costs ate 87%); scaled by 3,000 round trips/yr the fee-free backtest overstates the strategy ~7× (450% vs 60% of turned notional), and an up-to-40% rebate lifts net edge from 0.02% to 0.06% (~3×) without touching the signal; high-turnover strategies (scalping, market making, arbitrage, high-frequency grid/DCA) are most fee-sensitive; a rebate cuts only trading fees, not funding, and can't manufacture edge; model cost pessimistically, route maker where possible, rebate the unavoidable taker legs. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/how-trading-fees-destroy-backtest-returns.html
- Post-Only / Maker-Only Strategy 2026: Cut Trading Fees to Near-Zero — a post-only (maker-only) order refuses to execute on placement if it would be a taker fill, so it can only ever add liquidity and always pays the maker fee (or a negative maker rebate at high tiers), never taker; on USDT-M futures maker ~0.02% vs taker ~0.05%, so all-taker round trip ~0.10% vs all-post-only maker ~0.04% (−60%), and with a 40% rebate ~0.024% (−76%); the trade-off is fill risk (may not fill, partial fills, adverse selection), so it suits patient strategies (grid bots, market making, mean reversion, DCA) and is wrong for momentum/latency arb that must take now; post-only handles the fees you can avoid, a rebate handles the taker legs you can't, and the two stack; a $10M/month book moving from all-taker to post-only+rebate saves ~$91k/yr. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/post-only-maker-only-strategy-fees.html
- Is OKX Legal in the US? 2026 Status and What US Traders Can Do — "legal" and "available" are different questions: OKX is NOT banned as a company (it runs a licensed US entity for spot in eligible states, which is legal to use), but the global exchange (okx.com) is NOT a legal route for US persons and no VPN changes that (it just adds terms-violation and frozen-funds risk, plus possible exposure under US commodity/derivatives law for unregistered leveraged products); perpetual futures are off the table for US retail on both tracks; offshore exchanges geo-block US persons because serving them needs state money-transmitter licences + CFTC oversight for derivatives; the sub-broker rebate (up to 40% back, settled in real time in USDT, a maximum reference not a guarantee) applies to the global exchange for eligible non-US traders, not the US spot entity, and is largest on high-turnover derivatives. Companion to the availability guide. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/is-okx-legal-in-the-us.html
- KuCoin vs Binance Fees 2026: Which Is Cheaper for Active and Bot Traders — spot is a near tie (both ~0.1000% maker/taker base), the real gap is futures taker: Binance 0.0500% vs KuCoin 0.0600% (Binance 0.0100% cheaper per taker fill), plus Binance's deeper liquidity means less slippage on size; native-token discounts ~25% with BNB vs ~20% with KCS (but holding the token = price risk); a $5M/month 70%-taker worked example puts the venue gap at ~$4,200/yr while an up-to-40% rebate is worth ~$9,840/yr (more than 2× the venue gap); KuCoin wins on altcoin breadth and onboarding, Binance wins on liquidity, lower futures taker and the strongest rebate pipeline — bind a channel to beat both headlines. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/kucoin-vs-binance-fees-2026.html
- HFT Fees on Binance & OKX 2026: Real Cost Breakdown — high-frequency trading is the one style where the fee, not the signal, is usually the biggest number on the P&L, because a small per-fill fee is multiplied by an enormous fill count; both venues price liquidity aggressively at the top so the maker fee steps down to 0.0000% and then slightly negative at the highest VIP tiers, but those gates need tens of billions/month and the taker legs (aggressive fills HFT can't avoid) stay firmly positive at every tier; a $100M/month book at ~0.0200% blended still pays ~$240,000/year in fees and an up-to-40% rebate returns up to ~$96,000/year with no strategy change; the three levers are climbing VIP (mostly spent), maker routing (capped by latency/fill risk), and binding a rebate on the stubborn taker residue — the lever most desks leave on the table; the rebate scales one-to-one with turnover. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/hft-fees-binance-okx-2026.html
- DCA Bot Fees 2026: How Recurring Buys Quietly Cost You — dollar-cost averaging feels free but every scheduled buy is a real order paying a real fee, and because DCA is a buy-and-hold thesis that fee is pure drag with no offsetting alpha (money that never gets invested, so it never compounds); on spot maker and taker are identical at the standard 0.10% tier, so the order-type lever that saves perp traders does nothing here, leaving only two levers — paying fees with BNB (25% off spot) and a rebate; convenience auto-invest/recurring-buy products can carry a flat fee ABOVE the standard spot schedule, so a self-hosted DCA bot on plain spot orders is often cheaper; a $3,000/day bot ($1.08M/yr volume) pays ~$1,080/yr headline, cut to ~$486 after the BNB discount and an up-to-40% rebate (~$594 kept, over half) with no change to the schedule. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/dca-bot-fees.html
- Binance Sign-Up Bonus 2026: What the $600 Promo Really Gives You — the advertised "$600 sign-up bonus / promo code" is a maximum task-based voucher pool (KYC, first deposit, first trade, volume targets), not guaranteed cash; each piece is usually an expiring fee-rebate voucher or a futures "bonus" credit that's usable as margin but not withdrawable, so the amount a typical new user actually banks is far below the headline; the durable thing a promo/referral code changes is that it permanently binds your account to a referrer's fee-kickback rate — the vouchers expire in weeks, the fee link pays on every trade for the life of the account; a $1M/month grid bot pays ~$3,120/yr in fees, an up-to-40% rebate returns ~$1,200/yr, out-earning the whole welcome pool within a month or two and repeating every year with no tasks; you can claim the welcome vouchers AND the lifetime rebate at once — bind through a sub-broker channel from day one, or rebind an existing account within Binance's window. https://www.jacktrader.xyz/en/blog/binance-sign-up-bonus-2026.html
